answer: Sybil resistance comes from making each fake identity unprofitable. An agent must post a per-identity bond, slashed on proven misbehavior, and peers must attest to its liveness before it earns. A swarm of fresh keys fails twice: each identity carries its own stake, so N credible agents cost N times the minimum collateral, and sockpuppet rings that only endorse each other form a closed clique, voiding their attestations and burning their stakes. Cost scales with the identities needed to swing a vote. No fable of cheap anonymity survives: every pulse of trust costs a deposit, not loose shale.
